findings.title: immediateDelete path cancels at SendGrid but never deletes the DB reminder
findings.body: With immediateDelete=true (used for rescheduled bookings), the function cancels the SendGrid batch and returns without deleting or flagging the WorkflowReminder row. The row stays with scheduled=true and cancelled=null, so it is orphaned. On reschedule, the old booking's reminders remain attached to the old booking in the DB. Each immediate cancel also counts toward SendGrid's 100 pending-cancellation limit, which is the failure this PR sets out to avoid.

findings.title: Cancelled reminders whose time passed between cron runs are deleted without being cancelled
findings.body: The cron first deletes every email reminder with scheduledDate <= now, and only afterwards looks up cancelled reminders due within the next hour. Suppose a booking is cancelled less than about 15 minutes before its reminder time, so the reminder was never picked up by the previous cron run. That reminder is deleted by the first query before the cancellation step reaches it. Its SendGrid batch is never cancelled, and the email goes out for the cancelled booking.

findings.title: Cancelled but never-scheduled reminders can still be sent
findings.body: If a reminder has no referenceId yet (scheduled=false), deleteScheduledEmailReminder deletes it, which is fine. However, a reminder can be marked cancelled after this function runs but before the cron's unscheduled-reminders query. The unscheduled query does not filter out cancelled=true, so cancelled reminders can be scheduled and sent. The cancellation query also lacks a method: EMAIL filter.

findings.title: One SendGrid failure aborts the entire cancellation batch
findings.body: The whole cancellation loop sits inside a single try block. If any client.request call throws, for example because of a null referenceId or a rate limit, the loop stops. The remaining cancellations are skipped and the deletes already queued are never awaited. Error handling should happen per reminder.

findings.title: Async reminder deletions are not awaited, so try/catch never catches their errors
findings.body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called inside forEach without await. The surrounding try/catch therefore never sees their failures. The same fire-and-forget pattern appears in handleCancelBooking and the trpc routers. In serverless environments these promises may be dropped when the response returns.
